**Laurence Rickard** is an English actor, writer, and comedian best known as a member of the Them There collective, with whom he both wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. In 2022, along with fellow Them There member Ben Willbond, he co-wrote the feature length television comedy [_We Are Not Alone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Not_Alone_(2022_film) "We Are Not Alone (2022 film)").

He is also one half of the comedy writing/performance duo "Larry and George" with [George Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Sawyer_(comedian) "George Sawyer (comedian)").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Laurence_Rickard&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

Rickard has written for UK comedy shows including _[The Armstrong and Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Armstrong\_and\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong and Miller Show")_, _[The Charlotte Church Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Charlotte\_Church\_Show "The Charlotte Church Show")_ and _[The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Impressions\_Show\_with\_Culshaw\_and\_Stephenson "The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson")_, as well as children's programme _[Me and My Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me\_and\_My\_Monsters "Me and My Monsters")_.

He is a principal cast member, lyricist and writer for the award-winning [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBBC "CBBC") programme _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, in particular creating and performing the character of 'Special Correspondent' Bob Hale (a parody of presenter [Peter Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Snow "Peter Snow")).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-2) He has also appeared regularly on the spin-off game show _[Horrible Histories: Gory Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories:\_Gory\_Games "Horrible Histories: Gory Games")_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-3) and in the _Horrible Histories_[BBC Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Proms "BBC Proms") at the Royal Albert Hall.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-4)

Along with the five other members of the _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ starring cast, Rickard is also the co-creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family/fantasy/comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013. A second series was released in 2015 and a third was commissioned and began filming in early 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-5) In addition he is the co-writer of _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film which is based loosely around the early life of William Shakespeare and involves the same starring troupe.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-6) Filming took place in 2014, and the film had a nationwide UK release in September 2015.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-7)

As a performer, Rickard has also appeared in the Channel Four [Comedy Lab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_Lab "Comedy Lab")_Private Lives_ as well as the TV series _[Balls of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balls\_of\_Steel\_(TV\_series) "Balls of Steel (TV series)")_. He is also a writer and performer on _[Tracey Ullman's Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracey\_Ullman's\_Show "Tracey Ullman's Show")_[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-8) and _[Tracey Breaks the News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracey\_Breaks\_the\_News "Tracey Breaks the News")_. Rickard co-created, wrote, and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_ (2019-2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1) and is co-writer of the BBC sitcom _[Amandaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amandaland "Amandaland")_ (2025-2026).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-9)

In 2024, Rickard was awarded an honorary doctorate in humanities from [Brunel University London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunel_University_London "Brunel University London") for his services to television and education.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1)

**Laurence Rickard** is an English actor, writer, and comedian best known as a member of the Them There collective, with whom he both wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. In 2022, along with fellow Them There member Ben Willbond, he co-wrote the feature length television comedy [_We Are Not Alone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Not_Alone_(2022_film) "We Are Not Alone (2022 film)").

He is also one half of the comedy writing/performance duo "Larry and George" with [George Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Sawyer_(comedian) "George Sawyer (comedian)").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Laurence_Rickard&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

Rickard has written for UK comedy shows including _[The Armstrong and Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Armstrong\_and\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong and Miller Show")_, _[The Charlotte Church Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Charlotte\_Church\_Show "The Charlotte Church Show")_ and _[The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Impressions\_Show\_with\_Culshaw\_and\_Stephenson "The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson")_, as well as children's programme _[Me and My Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me\_and\_My\_Monsters "Me and My Monsters")_.

He is a principal cast member, lyricist and writer for the award-winning [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBBC "CBBC") programme _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, in particular creating and performing the character of 'Special Correspondent' Bob Hale (a parody of presenter [Peter Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Snow "Peter Snow")).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-2) He has also appeared regularly on the spin-off game show _[Horrible Histories: Gory Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories:\_Gory\_Games "Horrible Histories: Gory Games")_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-3) and in the _Horrible Histories_[BBC Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Proms "BBC Proms") at the Royal Albert Hall.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-4)

Along with the five other members of the _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ starring cast, Rickard is also the co-creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family/fantasy/comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013. A second series was released in 2015 and a third was commissioned and began filming in early 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-5) In addition he is the co-writer of _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film which is based loosely around the early life of William Shakespeare and involves the same starring troupe.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-6) Filming took place in 2014, and the film had a nationwide UK release in September 2015.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-7)

As a performer, Rickard has also appeared in the Channel Four [Comedy Lab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_Lab "Comedy Lab")_Private Lives_ as well as the TV series _[Balls of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balls\_of\_Steel\_(TV\_series) "Balls of Steel (TV series)")_. He is also a writer and performer on _[Tracey Ullman's Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracey\_Ullman's\_Show "Tracey Ullman's Show")_[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-8) and _[Tracey Breaks the News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracey\_Breaks\_the\_News "Tracey Breaks the News")_. Rickard co-created, wrote, and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_ (2019-2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1) and is co-writer of the BBC sitcom _[Amandaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amandaland "Amandaland")_ (2025-2026).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-9)

In 2024, Rickard was awarded an honorary doctorate in humanities from [Brunel University London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunel_University_London "Brunel University London") for his services to television and education.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1)

**Laurence Rickard** is an English actor, writer, and comedian best known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective, with whom he both wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. In 2022, along with fellow Them There member [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond"), he co-wrote the feature length television comedy [_We Are Not Alone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/We_Are_Not_Alone_(2022_film) "We Are Not Alone (2022 film)").

He is also one half of the comedy writing/performance duo "Larry and George" with [George Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/George_Sawyer_(comedian) "George Sawyer (comedian)").

## Career

Rickard has written for UK comedy shows including _[The Armstrong and Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_and\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong and Miller Show")_, _[The Charlotte Church Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Charlotte\_Church\_Show "The Charlotte Church Show")_ and _[The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Impressions\_Show\_with\_Culshaw\_and\_Stephenson "The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson")_, as well as children's programme _[Me and My Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Me\_and\_My\_Monsters "Me and My Monsters")_.

He is a principal cast member, lyricist and writer for the award-winning [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC") programme _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, in particular creating and performing the character of 'Special Correspondent' Bob Hale (a parody of presenter [Peter Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Peter_Snow "Peter Snow")).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-2) He has also appeared regularly on the spin-off game show _[Horrible Histories: Gory Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories:\_Gory\_Games "Horrible Histories: Gory Games")_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-3) and in the _Horrible Histories_[BBC Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_Proms "BBC Proms") at the Royal Albert Hall.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-4)

Along with the five other members of the _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ starring cast, Rickard is also the co-creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family/fantasy/comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013. A second series was released in 2015 and a third was commissioned and began filming in early 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-5) In addition he is the co-writer of _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film which is based loosely around the early life of William Shakespeare and involves the same starring troupe.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-6) Filming took place in 2014, and the film had a nationwide UK release in September 2015.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-7)

As a performer, Rickard has also appeared in the Channel Four [Comedy Lab](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy_Lab "Comedy Lab")_Private Lives_ as well as the TV series _[Balls of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Balls\_of\_Steel\_(TV\_series) "Balls of Steel (TV series)")_. He is also a writer and performer on _[Tracey Ullman's Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Ullman's\_Show "Tracey Ullman's Show")_[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-8) and _[Tracey Breaks the News](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Breaks\_the\_News "Tracey Breaks the News")_. Rickard co-created, wrote, and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_ (2019-2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1) and is co-writer of the BBC sitcom _[Amandaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Amandaland "Amandaland")_ (2025-2026).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-9)

In 2024, Rickard was awarded an honorary doctorate in humanities from [Brunel University London](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Brunel_University_London "Brunel University London") for his services to television and education.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1)

**Laurence Rickard** is an English actor, writer, and comedian best known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective, with whom he both wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. In 2022, along with fellow Them There member [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond"), he co-wrote the feature length television comedy [_We Are Not Alone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/We_Are_Not_Alone_(2022_film) "We Are Not Alone (2022 film)").

He is also one half of the comedy writing/performance duo "Larry and George" with [George Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/George_Sawyer_(comedian) "George Sawyer (comedian)").

## Career

Rickard has written for UK comedy shows including _[The Armstrong and Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_and\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong and Miller Show")_, _[The Charlotte Church Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Charlotte\_Church\_Show "The Charlotte Church Show")_ and _[The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Impressions\_Show\_with\_Culshaw\_and\_Stephenson "The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson")_, as well as children's programme _[Me and My Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Me\_and\_My\_Monsters "Me and My Monsters")_.

He is a principal cast member, lyricist and writer for the award-winning [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC") programme _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, in particular creating and performing the character of 'Special Correspondent' Bob Hale (a parody of presenter [Peter Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Peter_Snow "Peter Snow")).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-2) He has also appeared regularly on the spin-off game show _[Horrible Histories: Gory Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories:\_Gory\_Games "Horrible Histories: Gory Games")_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-3) and in the _Horrible Histories_[BBC Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_Proms "BBC Proms") at the Royal Albert Hall.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-4)

Along with the five other members of the _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ starring cast, Rickard is also the co-creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family/fantasy/comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013. A second series was released in 2015 and a third was commissioned and began filming in early 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-5) In addition he is the co-writer of _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film which is based loosely around the early life of William Shakespeare and involves the same starring troupe.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-6) Filming took place in 2014, and the film had a nationwide UK release in September 2015.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-7)

As a performer, Rickard has also appeared in the Channel Four [Comedy Lab](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy_Lab "Comedy Lab")_Private Lives_ as well as the TV series _[Balls of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Balls\_of\_Steel\_(TV\_series) "Balls of Steel (TV series)")_. He is also a writer and performer on _[Tracey Ullman's Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Ullman's\_Show "Tracey Ullman's Show")_[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-8) and _[Tracey Breaks the News](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Breaks\_the\_News "Tracey Breaks the News")_. Rickard co-created, wrote, and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_ (2019-2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1) and is co-writer of the BBC sitcom _[Amandaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Amandaland "Amandaland")_ (2025-2026).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-9)

In 2024, Rickard was awarded an honorary doctorate in humanities from [Brunel University London](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Brunel_University_London "Brunel University London") for his services to television and education.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1)

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)

**Simon Farnaby** (born 2 April 1973) is an English actor, comedian, writer and singer. He is best known for his work with the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective where he has written and starred in productions including the sketch show [_Horrible Histories_](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Horrible_Histories_(2009_TV_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)"), _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and [_Ghosts_](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ghosts_(2019_British_TV_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)"), as well as writing for film.

Farnaby earned [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTA "BAFTA") nominations for his writing of _[Paddington 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Paddington\_2 "Paddington 2")_, both for [Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "BAFTA Award for Best Adapted Screenplay") and [Best British Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTA_Award_for_Outstanding_British_Film "BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-1) and was the winner of the 2023 [Television BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2) In 2023, he co-wrote and appeared in _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_, a film which serves as a prequel to the [Roald Dahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Roald_Dahl "Roald Dahl") novel _[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Charlie\_and\_the\_Chocolate\_Factory "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory")_, exploring [Willy Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Willy_Wonka "Willy Wonka")'s origins.

## Early life

Farnaby was born on 2 April 1973 in [Darlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Darlington "Darlington"), [County Durham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/County_Durham "County Durham")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-3) and attended [Richmond School](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Richmond_School "Richmond School"), [North Yorkshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/North_Yorkshire "North Yorkshire").

## Career

### Television work

Farnaby was a long-time member of _[The Mighty Boosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Mighty\_Boosh "The Mighty Boosh")_ supporting cast,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-metro-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-ie-5) having had roles both in their series and co-starring in the quasi-spinoff film _[Bunny and the Bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bunny\_and\_the\_Bull "Bunny and the Bull")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-bunny-6)

Other notable television work includes recurring roles in the sitcoms _[Jam & Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Jam\_&\_Jerusalem "Jam & Jerusalem")_,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)_[The Midnight Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Midnight\_Beast\_(TV\_series) "The Midnight Beast (TV series)")_[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-metro-4) and _[Detectorists](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Detectorists "Detectorists")_. He previously had a very brief role in one episode of _[Coronation Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Coronation\_Street "Coronation Street")_ in the 1990s.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)

Farnaby has presented a number of factual programmes including _Richard III: The King in the Car Park_ in 2013,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-8) tracing the [discovery and identification](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Exhumation_of_Richard_III_of_England "Exhumation of Richard III of England") of the remains of the last [Plantagenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Plantagenet "Plantagenet") king, the 2014 Channel 4 documentary series entitled _Man Vs Weird_, in which he travelled the world investigating people who claim superhuman abilities,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-9) and as narrator of the [Channel 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Channel_5_(UK) "Channel 5 (UK)") docu-series called _[On the Yorkshire Buses](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/On\_the\_Yorkshire\_Buses "On the Yorkshire Buses")_, following [East Yorkshire Motor Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/East_Yorkshire_Motor_Services "East Yorkshire Motor Services").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-10)

Farnaby accepted a [TV BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") in 2023 for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment"), for a short film broadcast as part of the [Platinum Party at the Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Platinum_Party_at_the_Palace "Platinum Party at the Palace") for the [Platinum Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Platinum_Jubilee_of_Elizabeth_II "Platinum Jubilee of Elizabeth II") of [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in June 2022, in which Farnaby played a butler.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2)

#### Them There

Main article: [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There")

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg/250px-The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/File:The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children's_BAFTAs,_27_November_2011.jpg)

L-R: Simon Farnaby, Martha Howe-Douglas, [Mathew Baynton](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton "Mathew Baynton"), Laurence Rickard, [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond") and [Jim Howick](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Jim_Howick "Jim Howick") at the 2011 Children's [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTAs "BAFTAs").

Farnaby has worked extensively with the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective of six writers and actors, who started as principal members of the cast of the [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC") live-action series _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, where he played offbeat characters including [Caligula](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Caligula "Caligula") and Death.

Farnaby, along with the five other collective members, co-created, wrote and starred in _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ (2013–2016),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-11) which was broadcast on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One") for three series.

Farnaby had his first major involvement with the creation of a film with the troupe, on the 2015 historical comedy film _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, based loosely around the early life of [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-13)

The same collective then went on to create the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") show _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_, which ran for five seasons before the team decided to retire it.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-14) Farnaby played the fictitious [Conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Conservative_Party_(UK) "Conservative Party (UK)") politician ghost, Julian Fawcett,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-15) who always appeared without trousers.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)

### Books

Along with journalist Scott Murray, in 2011 Farnaby co-wrote _[The Phantom of the Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Phantom\_of\_the\_Open "The Phantom of the Open")_, a biography of [Maurice Flitcroft](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Maurice_Flitcroft "Maurice Flitcroft"), a would-be professional golfer whose unsuccessful attempts to qualify for the [Open Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Open_Championship "Open Championship") led to his being described as "the world's worst golfer".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-chortle-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-17)

His first children's novel, _The Wizard In My Shed_, was published in 2020,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-18) and this was followed by a sequel titled _Warrior in my Wardrobe: More Misadventures with Merdyn the Wild_, which was released in 2021.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-20)

Farnaby was also a co-author of _Ghosts: The Button House Archives_, a companion book to the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") television series for the BBC, _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_ which he co-wrote and starred in.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-22)

### Films

Having previously appeared in _[The Mighty Boosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Mighty\_Boosh "The Mighty Boosh")_, Farnaby was in a starring role for the related film _[Bunny and the Bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bunny\_and\_the\_Bull "Bunny and the Bull")_ in 2009, where he played the eponymous Bunny.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-bunny-6)

In 2016, Farnaby co-wrote and had a small acting part in _[Mindhorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Mindhorn "Mindhorn")_ with [Julian Barratt](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Julian_Barratt "Julian Barratt"), a comedy about Richard Thorncroft (Barratt), a faded television actor drawn into negotiations with a criminal who believes his character Detective Mindhorn is real.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-ie-5)

He co-wrote the book _The Phantom of the Open_ about golfer [Maurice Flitcroft](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Maurice_Flitcroft "Maurice Flitcroft") in 2011, and then started work on a film script of the story in 2017, which led to the release of _[The Phantom of the Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Phantom\_of\_the\_Open "The Phantom of the Open")_ in 2021, starring [Mark Rylance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mark_Rylance "Mark Rylance").

Also in 2016, Farnaby had a small on-screen role in _[Rogue One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Rogue\_One "Rogue One")_, as an X-Wing pilot.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-23)

The biggest film success of Farnaby's career came with the [Paddington](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paddington_(film) "Paddington (film)") film franchise. Following on from appearing as an actor in [the first film](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paddington_(film) "Paddington (film)"), he went on to co-write _[Paddington 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Paddington\_2 "Paddington 2")_ with [Paul King](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paul_King_(director) "Paul King (director)"), for which he was nominated for two [film BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards") for [best adapted screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "BAFTA Award for Best Adapted Screenplay") and [Outstanding British Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTA_Award_for_Outstanding_British_Film "BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film"). He was also the winner of the International Online Cinema Award for Best Adapted Screenplay, and the [Hollywood Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Hollywood_Critics_Association "Hollywood Critics Association") award for Best Adapted Screenplay in 2018.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-24) Farnaby subsequently appeared alongside [Paddington Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paddington_Bear "Paddington Bear") and [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in a short film broadcast as a part of the [Platinum Party at the Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Platinum_Party_at_the_Palace "Platinum Party at the Palace") for the [Platinum Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Platinum_Jubilee_of_Elizabeth_II "Platinum Jubilee of Elizabeth II") of [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in June 2022, which won the 2023 [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment"), which Farnaby accepted.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2)

Farnaby is the co-writer of 2023 Christmas release _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_, along with [Paul King](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paul_King_(director) "Paul King (director)"), which is a prequel to _[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Charlie\_and\_the\_Chocolate\_Factory "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory")_ by [Roald Dahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Roald_Dahl "Roald Dahl").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-25) Alongside _Ghosts_ co-star [Charlotte Ritchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Charlotte_Ritchie "Charlotte Ritchie"), Farnaby also has a small on-screen role, with his [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collaborator [Mathew Baynton](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton "Mathew Baynton") in one of the leading roles, and starring [Timothée Chalamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Timoth%C3%A9e_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet").

Farnaby wrote the screenplay for [The Magic Faraway Tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/The_Magic_Faraway_Tree_(film) "The Magic Faraway Tree (film)").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-26) An adaptation of [Enid Blyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Enid_Blyton "Enid Blyton")'s book series of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/The_Faraway_Tree "The Faraway Tree"). The film released theatrically in the UK on 27 March 2026.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-27)

## Personal life

Farnaby is married to actress [Claire Keelan](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Claire_Keelan "Claire Keelan") (his second wife) with whom he has a daughter, born in 2014.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-28)

**Simon Farnaby** (born 2 April 1973) is an English actor, comedian, writer and singer. He is best known for his work with the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective where he has written and starred in productions including the sketch show [_Horrible Histories_](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Horrible_Histories_(2009_TV_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)"), _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and [_Ghosts_](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ghosts_(2019_British_TV_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)"), as well as writing for film.

Farnaby earned [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTA "BAFTA") nominations for his writing of _[Paddington 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Paddington\_2 "Paddington 2")_, both for [Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "BAFTA Award for Best Adapted Screenplay") and [Best British Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTA_Award_for_Outstanding_British_Film "BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-1) and was the winner of the 2023 [Television BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2) In 2023, he co-wrote and appeared in _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_, a film which serves as a prequel to the [Roald Dahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Roald_Dahl "Roald Dahl") novel _[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Charlie\_and\_the\_Chocolate\_Factory "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory")_, exploring [Willy Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Willy_Wonka "Willy Wonka")'s origins.

## Early life

Farnaby was born on 2 April 1973 in [Darlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Darlington "Darlington"), [County Durham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/County_Durham "County Durham")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-3) and attended [Richmond School](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Richmond_School "Richmond School"), [North Yorkshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/North_Yorkshire "North Yorkshire").

## Career

### Television work

Farnaby was a long-time member of _[The Mighty Boosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Mighty\_Boosh "The Mighty Boosh")_ supporting cast,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-metro-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-ie-5) having had roles both in their series and co-starring in the quasi-spinoff film _[Bunny and the Bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bunny\_and\_the\_Bull "Bunny and the Bull")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-bunny-6)

Other notable television work includes recurring roles in the sitcoms _[Jam & Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Jam\_&\_Jerusalem "Jam & Jerusalem")_,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)_[The Midnight Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Midnight\_Beast\_(TV\_series) "The Midnight Beast (TV series)")_[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-metro-4) and _[Detectorists](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Detectorists "Detectorists")_. He previously had a very brief role in one episode of _[Coronation Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Coronation\_Street "Coronation Street")_ in the 1990s.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)

Farnaby has presented a number of factual programmes including _Richard III: The King in the Car Park_ in 2013,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-8) tracing the [discovery and identification](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Exhumation_of_Richard_III_of_England "Exhumation of Richard III of England") of the remains of the last [Plantagenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Plantagenet "Plantagenet") king, the 2014 Channel 4 documentary series entitled _Man Vs Weird_, in which he travelled the world investigating people who claim superhuman abilities,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-9) and as narrator of the [Channel 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Channel_5_(UK) "Channel 5 (UK)") docu-series called _[On the Yorkshire Buses](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/On\_the\_Yorkshire\_Buses "On the Yorkshire Buses")_, following [East Yorkshire Motor Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/East_Yorkshire_Motor_Services "East Yorkshire Motor Services").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-10)

Farnaby accepted a [TV BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") in 2023 for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment"), for a short film broadcast as part of the [Platinum Party at the Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Platinum_Party_at_the_Palace "Platinum Party at the Palace") for the [Platinum Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Platinum_Jubilee_of_Elizabeth_II "Platinum Jubilee of Elizabeth II") of [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in June 2022, in which Farnaby played a butler.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2)

#### Them There

Main article: [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There")

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg/250px-The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/File:The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children's_BAFTAs,_27_November_2011.jpg)

L-R: Simon Farnaby, Martha Howe-Douglas, [Mathew Baynton](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton "Mathew Baynton"), Laurence Rickard, [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond") and [Jim Howick](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Jim_Howick "Jim Howick") at the 2011 Children's [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTAs "BAFTAs").

Farnaby has worked extensively with the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective of six writers and actors, who started as principal members of the cast of the [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC") live-action series _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, where he played offbeat characters including [Caligula](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Caligula "Caligula") and Death.

Farnaby, along with the five other collective members, co-created, wrote and starred in _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ (2013–2016),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-11) which was broadcast on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One") for three series.

Farnaby had his first major involvement with the creation of a film with the troupe, on the 2015 historical comedy film _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, based loosely around the early life of [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-13)

The same collective then went on to create the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") show _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_, which ran for five seasons before the team decided to retire it.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-14) Farnaby played the fictitious [Conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Conservative_Party_(UK) "Conservative Party (UK)") politician ghost, Julian Fawcett,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-15) who always appeared without trousers.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)

### Books

Along with journalist Scott Murray, in 2011 Farnaby co-wrote _[The Phantom of the Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Phantom\_of\_the\_Open "The Phantom of the Open")_, a biography of [Maurice Flitcroft](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Maurice_Flitcroft "Maurice Flitcroft"), a would-be professional golfer whose unsuccessful attempts to qualify for the [Open Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Open_Championship "Open Championship") led to his being described as "the world's worst golfer".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-chortle-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-17)

His first children's novel, _The Wizard In My Shed_, was published in 2020,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-18) and this was followed by a sequel titled _Warrior in my Wardrobe: More Misadventures with Merdyn the Wild_, which was released in 2021.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-20)

Farnaby was also a co-author of _Ghosts: The Button House Archives_, a companion book to the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") television series for the BBC, _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_ which he co-wrote and starred in.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-22)

### Films

Having previously appeared in _[The Mighty Boosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Mighty\_Boosh "The Mighty Boosh")_, Farnaby was in a starring role for the related film _[Bunny and the Bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bunny\_and\_the\_Bull "Bunny and the Bull")_ in 2009, where he played the eponymous Bunny.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-bunny-6)

In 2016, Farnaby co-wrote and had a small acting part in _[Mindhorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Mindhorn "Mindhorn")_ with [Julian Barratt](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Julian_Barratt "Julian Barratt"), a comedy about Richard Thorncroft (Barratt), a faded television actor drawn into negotiations with a criminal who believes his character Detective Mindhorn is real.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-ie-5)

He co-wrote the book _The Phantom of the Open_ about golfer [Maurice Flitcroft](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Maurice_Flitcroft "Maurice Flitcroft") in 2011, and then started work on a film script of the story in 2017, which led to the release of _[The Phantom of the Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Phantom\_of\_the\_Open "The Phantom of the Open")_ in 2021, starring [Mark Rylance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mark_Rylance "Mark Rylance").

Also in 2016, Farnaby had a small on-screen role in _[Rogue One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Rogue\_One "Rogue One")_, as an X-Wing pilot.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-23)

The biggest film success of Farnaby's career came with the [Paddington](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paddington_(film) "Paddington (film)") film franchise. Following on from appearing as an actor in [the first film](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paddington_(film) "Paddington (film)"), he went on to co-write _[Paddington 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Paddington\_2 "Paddington 2")_ with [Paul King](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paul_King_(director) "Paul King (director)"), for which he was nominated for two [film BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards") for [best adapted screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "BAFTA Award for Best Adapted Screenplay") and [Outstanding British Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTA_Award_for_Outstanding_British_Film "BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film"). He was also the winner of the International Online Cinema Award for Best Adapted Screenplay, and the [Hollywood Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Hollywood_Critics_Association "Hollywood Critics Association") award for Best Adapted Screenplay in 2018.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-24) Farnaby subsequently appeared alongside [Paddington Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paddington_Bear "Paddington Bear") and [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in a short film broadcast as a part of the [Platinum Party at the Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Platinum_Party_at_the_Palace "Platinum Party at the Palace") for the [Platinum Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Platinum_Jubilee_of_Elizabeth_II "Platinum Jubilee of Elizabeth II") of [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in June 2022, which won the 2023 [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment"), which Farnaby accepted.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2)

Farnaby is the co-writer of 2023 Christmas release _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_, along with [Paul King](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paul_King_(director) "Paul King (director)"), which is a prequel to _[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Charlie\_and\_the\_Chocolate\_Factory "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory")_ by [Roald Dahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Roald_Dahl "Roald Dahl").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-25) Alongside _Ghosts_ co-star [Charlotte Ritchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Charlotte_Ritchie "Charlotte Ritchie"), Farnaby also has a small on-screen role, with his [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collaborator [Mathew Baynton](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton "Mathew Baynton") in one of the leading roles, and starring [Timothée Chalamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Timoth%C3%A9e_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet").

Farnaby wrote the screenplay for [The Magic Faraway Tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/The_Magic_Faraway_Tree_(film) "The Magic Faraway Tree (film)").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-26) An adaptation of [Enid Blyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Enid_Blyton "Enid Blyton")'s book series of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/The_Faraway_Tree "The Faraway Tree"). The film released theatrically in the UK on 27 March 2026.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-27)

## Personal life

Farnaby is married to actress [Claire Keelan](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Claire_Keelan "Claire Keelan") (his second wife) with whom he has a daughter, born in 2014.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-28)
