**Mathew John Baynton** is an English actor, comedian, musician and writer. He is a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There")[collective](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Collective "Collective"), in which he wrote and starred in _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. He was also the co-creator, writer and star of the [comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy_drama "Comedy drama")_[The Wrong Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Wrong\_Mans "The Wrong Mans")_. Other television roles include Elliot Ward in _[A Good Girl's Guide to Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/A\_Good\_Girl's\_Guide\_to\_Murder\_(TV\_series) "A Good Girl's Guide to Murder (TV series)")_, Deano in _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_, Chris Pitt-Goddard in _[Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Spy\_(2011\_TV\_series) "Spy (2011 TV series)")_, Simon in _[Peep Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Peep\_Show\_(British\_TV\_series) "Peep Show (British TV series)")_, William Agar in _[Quacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Quacks\_(TV\_series) "Quacks (TV series)")_, and twin brothers Jamie Winton and Ariel Conroy in _[You, Me and the Apocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/You,\_Me\_and\_the\_Apocalypse "You, Me and the Apocalypse")_. He has appeared in several films, including _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_ (2015) and _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_ (2023).

## Early life and education

Mathew Baynton grew up in [Southend-on-Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Southend-on-Sea "Southend-on-Sea"), Essex.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-theprotagonistmagazine_mathew-baynton-1)He is the youngest of three boys, with two older brothers, Daniel and Andrew.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-cc-2)

He was educated at [Southend High School for Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Southend_High_School_for_Boys "Southend High School for Boys"). He graduated with [first class honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/First_class_honours "First class honours") from the [Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Rose_Bruford_College_of_Speech_and_Drama "Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-cc-2) and later trained in [clowning](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Clown "Clown") at [École Philippe Gaulier](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Philippe_Gaulier "Philippe Gaulier") in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paris "Paris").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-3)

Baynton's second cousins [Daisy May Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Daisy_May_Cooper "Daisy May Cooper") and [Charlie Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Charlie_Cooper_(actor) "Charlie Cooper (actor)") are also in the acting profession.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-4)[Trevor Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Trevor_Cooper "Trevor Cooper") is his first cousin once removed.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-5)

## Career

### Acting and writing

Baynton is one of the performers of the children's television series _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, appearing in the first five series as an actor, singer, and occasional writer.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-TelWest-6) Baynton and the other five members of the main _Horrible Histories_ cast form the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") troupe, which has since created other shows.

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg/500px-The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/File:The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children's_BAFTAs,_27_November_2011.jpg)

L-R: Simon Farnaby, Martha Howe-Douglas, Mathew Baynton, Laurence Rickard, [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond") and [Jim Howick](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Jim_Howick "Jim Howick") at the 2011 Children's [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTAs "BAFTAs").

Along with the other members of the troupe, Baynton is the creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family fantasy comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-7) He starred with the same troupe in _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC")[family comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sitcom "Sitcom") film based loosely around the early life of [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare"), who ventures to [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/London "London") to pursue his dream of becoming a [playwright](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Playwright "Playwright").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-9) The troupe also reunited in 2019 to create the BBC series _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, with Baynton appearing as a [Romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Romanticism "Romanticism") poet named Thomas Thorne.

Baynton teamed with friend and fellow _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_ alumnus [James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/James_Corden "James Corden") to create, write, and star in _[The Wrong Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Wrong\_Mans "The Wrong Mans")_, a [comedy thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy_thriller "Comedy thriller") for [BBC Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_Two "BBC Two") that premiered in autumn 2013.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-10) The series is co-produced by online television provider [Hulu.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Hulu.com "Hulu.com") in the United States, where it premiered in November 2013.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-11) The first six-part series proved a critical and commercial success, and a similarly well-received two-part sequel was broadcast in December 2014.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-12)

Other notable TV comedy roles include Deano in _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_; Chris in the [Darren Boyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Darren_Boyd "Darren Boyd") sitcom vehicle _[Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Spy\_(2011\_TV\_series) "Spy (2011 TV series)")_; and William in the 2017 [black comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Black_comedy "Black comedy") series _[Quacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Quacks\_(TV\_series) "Quacks (TV series)")_.

In 2009, he appeared in a [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Music_video "Music video") for [Mercury Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mercury_Prize "Mercury Prize")-nominated band [The Bees](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/The_Bees_(English_band) "The Bees (English band)").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-13)

Baynton appeared at the 2013 [Edinburgh Fringe Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Edinburgh_Fringe_Festival "Edinburgh Fringe Festival"), starring in the world premiere of [Tom Basden](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Tom_Basden "Tom Basden")'s play _Holes_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-14) He reprised his role of Gus in a London revival of the same play in summer 2014.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-15)

In late 2015, Baynton portrayed Jamie Winton and his brother Ariel Conroy in [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One")'s [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Science_fiction "Science fiction")[comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy-drama "Comedy-drama") miniseries _[You, Me and the Apocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/You,\_Me\_and\_the\_Apocalypse "You, Me and the Apocalypse")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In January 2024, Baynton made his [Royal Shakespeare Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company") debut in [Eleanor Rhode](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Eleanor_Rhode "Eleanor Rhode")'s production of _[A Midsummer Night's Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/A\_Midsummer\_Night's\_Dream "A Midsummer Night's Dream")_ as [Nick Bottom](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Nick_Bottom "Nick Bottom") at the [Royal Shakespeare Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Royal_Shakespeare_Theatre "Royal Shakespeare Theatre"), [Stratford-upon-Avon](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Stratford-upon-Avon "Stratford-upon-Avon"), before transferring to the [Barbican Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Barbican_Centre "Barbican Centre") in December 2024.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-17)

In January 2025, it was announced that Baynton would appear as a contestant on the nineteenth series of the [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Channel_4 "Channel 4") show _[Taskmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Taskmaster\_(TV\_series) "Taskmaster (TV series)")_ alongside [Fatiha El-Ghorri](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Fatiha_El-Ghorri "Fatiha El-Ghorri"), [Jason Mantzoukas](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Jason_Mantzoukas "Jason Mantzoukas"), [Rosie Ramsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Rosie_Ramsey "Rosie Ramsey"), and [Stevie Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Stevie_Martin "Stevie Martin").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-18) Baynton would go on to win the series. Bayton also participated in _[Taskmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Taskmaster\_(TV\_series) "Taskmaster (TV series)") Champion of Champions 4,_ which aired in December 2025. He won, beating [Andy Zaltzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Andy_Zaltzman "Andy Zaltzman"), [Maisie Adam](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Maisie_Adam "Maisie Adam"), [Sam Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sam_Campbell_(comedian) "Sam Campbell (comedian)") and [John Robins](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/John_Robins_(comedian) "John Robins (comedian)").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-19)

Baynton is a former member of the band Special Benny as a vocalist and guitarist.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-20) Their debut album _Toys_ was released in 2010.

## Personal life

Baynton and his partner Kelly Robinson, a [film historian](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/History_of_film "History of film"), have two children. Baynton and Robinson had a [civil partnership](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Civil_union "Civil union") ceremony in 2023.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-22)

Baynton said in a 2013 interview that he would be happy for his son to become an actor, if he enjoyed acting.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-:0-23) He tries to keep his children out of the spotlight; however, he raised awareness about breaking [gender stereotypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Gender_role "Gender role") after his son was mocked for wearing a pink bicycle helmet.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-:1-24)

**Mathew John Baynton** is an English actor, comedian, musician and writer. He is a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There")[collective](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Collective "Collective"), in which he wrote and starred in _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. He was also the co-creator, writer and star of the [comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy_drama "Comedy drama")_[The Wrong Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Wrong\_Mans "The Wrong Mans")_. Other television roles include Elliot Ward in _[A Good Girl's Guide to Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/A\_Good\_Girl's\_Guide\_to\_Murder\_(TV\_series) "A Good Girl's Guide to Murder (TV series)")_, Deano in _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_, Chris Pitt-Goddard in _[Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Spy\_(2011\_TV\_series) "Spy (2011 TV series)")_, Simon in _[Peep Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Peep\_Show\_(British\_TV\_series) "Peep Show (British TV series)")_, William Agar in _[Quacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Quacks\_(TV\_series) "Quacks (TV series)")_, and twin brothers Jamie Winton and Ariel Conroy in _[You, Me and the Apocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/You,\_Me\_and\_the\_Apocalypse "You, Me and the Apocalypse")_. He has appeared in several films, including _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_ (2015) and _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_ (2023).

## Early life and education

Mathew Baynton grew up in [Southend-on-Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Southend-on-Sea "Southend-on-Sea"), Essex.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-theprotagonistmagazine_mathew-baynton-1)He is the youngest of three boys, with two older brothers, Daniel and Andrew.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-cc-2)

He was educated at [Southend High School for Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Southend_High_School_for_Boys "Southend High School for Boys"). He graduated with [first class honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/First_class_honours "First class honours") from the [Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Rose_Bruford_College_of_Speech_and_Drama "Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-cc-2) and later trained in [clowning](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Clown "Clown") at [École Philippe Gaulier](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Philippe_Gaulier "Philippe Gaulier") in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Paris "Paris").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-3)

Baynton's second cousins [Daisy May Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Daisy_May_Cooper "Daisy May Cooper") and [Charlie Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Charlie_Cooper_(actor) "Charlie Cooper (actor)") are also in the acting profession.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-4)[Trevor Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Trevor_Cooper "Trevor Cooper") is his first cousin once removed.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-5)

## Career

### Acting and writing

Baynton is one of the performers of the children's television series _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, appearing in the first five series as an actor, singer, and occasional writer.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-TelWest-6) Baynton and the other five members of the main _Horrible Histories_ cast form the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") troupe, which has since created other shows.

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg/500px-The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/File:The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children's_BAFTAs,_27_November_2011.jpg)

L-R: Simon Farnaby, Martha Howe-Douglas, Mathew Baynton, Laurence Rickard, [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond") and [Jim Howick](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Jim_Howick "Jim Howick") at the 2011 Children's [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BAFTAs "BAFTAs").

Along with the other members of the troupe, Baynton is the creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family fantasy comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-7) He starred with the same troupe in _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC")[family comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sitcom "Sitcom") film based loosely around the early life of [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare"), who ventures to [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/London "London") to pursue his dream of becoming a [playwright](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Playwright "Playwright").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-9) The troupe also reunited in 2019 to create the BBC series _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, with Baynton appearing as a [Romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Romanticism "Romanticism") poet named Thomas Thorne.

Baynton teamed with friend and fellow _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_ alumnus [James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/James_Corden "James Corden") to create, write, and star in _[The Wrong Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Wrong\_Mans "The Wrong Mans")_, a [comedy thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy_thriller "Comedy thriller") for [BBC Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_Two "BBC Two") that premiered in autumn 2013.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-10) The series is co-produced by online television provider [Hulu.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Hulu.com "Hulu.com") in the United States, where it premiered in November 2013.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-11) The first six-part series proved a critical and commercial success, and a similarly well-received two-part sequel was broadcast in December 2014.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-12)

Other notable TV comedy roles include Deano in _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_; Chris in the [Darren Boyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Darren_Boyd "Darren Boyd") sitcom vehicle _[Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Spy\_(2011\_TV\_series) "Spy (2011 TV series)")_; and William in the 2017 [black comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Black_comedy "Black comedy") series _[Quacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Quacks\_(TV\_series) "Quacks (TV series)")_.

In 2009, he appeared in a [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Music_video "Music video") for [Mercury Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mercury_Prize "Mercury Prize")-nominated band [The Bees](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/The_Bees_(English_band) "The Bees (English band)").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-13)

Baynton appeared at the 2013 [Edinburgh Fringe Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Edinburgh_Fringe_Festival "Edinburgh Fringe Festival"), starring in the world premiere of [Tom Basden](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Tom_Basden "Tom Basden")'s play _Holes_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-14) He reprised his role of Gus in a London revival of the same play in summer 2014.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-15)

In late 2015, Baynton portrayed Jamie Winton and his brother Ariel Conroy in [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One")'s [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Science_fiction "Science fiction")[comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy-drama "Comedy-drama") miniseries _[You, Me and the Apocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/You,\_Me\_and\_the\_Apocalypse "You, Me and the Apocalypse")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In January 2024, Baynton made his [Royal Shakespeare Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company") debut in [Eleanor Rhode](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Eleanor_Rhode "Eleanor Rhode")'s production of _[A Midsummer Night's Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/A\_Midsummer\_Night's\_Dream "A Midsummer Night's Dream")_ as [Nick Bottom](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Nick_Bottom "Nick Bottom") at the [Royal Shakespeare Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Royal_Shakespeare_Theatre "Royal Shakespeare Theatre"), [Stratford-upon-Avon](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Stratford-upon-Avon "Stratford-upon-Avon"), before transferring to the [Barbican Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Barbican_Centre "Barbican Centre") in December 2024.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-17)

In January 2025, it was announced that Baynton would appear as a contestant on the nineteenth series of the [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Channel_4 "Channel 4") show _[Taskmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Taskmaster\_(TV\_series) "Taskmaster (TV series)")_ alongside [Fatiha El-Ghorri](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Fatiha_El-Ghorri "Fatiha El-Ghorri"), [Jason Mantzoukas](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Jason_Mantzoukas "Jason Mantzoukas"), [Rosie Ramsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Rosie_Ramsey "Rosie Ramsey"), and [Stevie Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Stevie_Martin "Stevie Martin").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-18) Baynton would go on to win the series. Bayton also participated in _[Taskmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Taskmaster\_(TV\_series) "Taskmaster (TV series)") Champion of Champions 4,_ which aired in December 2025. He won, beating [Andy Zaltzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Andy_Zaltzman "Andy Zaltzman"), [Maisie Adam](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Maisie_Adam "Maisie Adam"), [Sam Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sam_Campbell_(comedian) "Sam Campbell (comedian)") and [John Robins](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/John_Robins_(comedian) "John Robins (comedian)").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-19)

Baynton is a former member of the band Special Benny as a vocalist and guitarist.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-20) Their debut album _Toys_ was released in 2010.

He has also performed as a solo act under the name Dog Ears. His debut solo EP, _So It Goes_, was released in November 2011.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-21) It consists of four self-penned songs.

### Radio

He appeared in 'John Finnemore's Double Acts'.

## Personal life

Baynton and his partner Kelly Robinson, a [film historian](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/History_of_film "History of film"), have two children. Baynton and Robinson had a [civil partnership](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Civil_union "Civil union") ceremony in 2023.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-22)

Baynton said in a 2013 interview that he would be happy for his son to become an actor, if he enjoyed acting.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-:0-23) He tries to keep his children out of the spotlight; however, he raised awareness about breaking [gender stereotypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Gender_role "Gender role") after his son was mocked for wearing a pink bicycle helmet.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-:1-24)

**Laurence Rickard** is an English actor, writer, and comedian best known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective, with whom he both wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. In 2022, along with fellow Them There member [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond"), he co-wrote the feature length television comedy [_We Are Not Alone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/We_Are_Not_Alone_(2022_film) "We Are Not Alone (2022 film)").

He is also one half of the comedy writing/performance duo "Larry and George" with [George Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/George_Sawyer_(comedian) "George Sawyer (comedian)").

## Career

Rickard has written for UK comedy shows including _[The Armstrong and Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_and\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong and Miller Show")_, _[The Charlotte Church Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Charlotte\_Church\_Show "The Charlotte Church Show")_ and _[The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Impressions\_Show\_with\_Culshaw\_and\_Stephenson "The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson")_, as well as children's programme _[Me and My Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Me\_and\_My\_Monsters "Me and My Monsters")_.

He is a principal cast member, lyricist and writer for the award-winning [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC") programme _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, in particular creating and performing the character of 'Special Correspondent' Bob Hale (a parody of presenter [Peter Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Peter_Snow "Peter Snow")).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-2) He has also appeared regularly on the spin-off game show _[Horrible Histories: Gory Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories:\_Gory\_Games "Horrible Histories: Gory Games")_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-3) and in the _Horrible Histories_[BBC Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_Proms "BBC Proms") at the Royal Albert Hall.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-4)

Along with the five other members of the _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ starring cast, Rickard is also the co-creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family/fantasy/comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013. A second series was released in 2015 and a third was commissioned and began filming in early 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-5) In addition he is the co-writer of _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film which is based loosely around the early life of William Shakespeare and involves the same starring troupe.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-6) Filming took place in 2014, and the film had a nationwide UK release in September 2015.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-7)

As a performer, Rickard has also appeared in the Channel Four [Comedy Lab](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy_Lab "Comedy Lab")_Private Lives_ as well as the TV series _[Balls of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Balls\_of\_Steel\_(TV\_series) "Balls of Steel (TV series)")_. He is also a writer and performer on _[Tracey Ullman's Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Ullman's\_Show "Tracey Ullman's Show")_[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-8) and _[Tracey Breaks the News](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Breaks\_the\_News "Tracey Breaks the News")_. Rickard co-created, wrote, and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_ (2019-2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1) and is co-writer of the BBC sitcom _[Amandaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Amandaland "Amandaland")_ (2025-2026).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-9)

In 2024, Rickard was awarded an honorary doctorate in humanities from [Brunel University London](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Brunel_University_London "Brunel University London") for his services to television and education.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1)

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)

**Laurence Rickard** is an English actor, writer, and comedian best known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective, with whom he both wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. In 2022, along with fellow Them There member [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond"), he co-wrote the feature length television comedy [_We Are Not Alone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/We_Are_Not_Alone_(2022_film) "We Are Not Alone (2022 film)").

He is also one half of the comedy writing/performance duo "Larry and George" with [George Sawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/George_Sawyer_(comedian) "George Sawyer (comedian)").

## Career

Rickard has written for UK comedy shows including _[The Armstrong and Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_and\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong and Miller Show")_, _[The Charlotte Church Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Charlotte\_Church\_Show "The Charlotte Church Show")_ and _[The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Impressions\_Show\_with\_Culshaw\_and\_Stephenson "The Impressions Show with Culshaw and Stephenson")_, as well as children's programme _[Me and My Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Me\_and\_My\_Monsters "Me and My Monsters")_.

He is a principal cast member, lyricist and writer for the award-winning [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC") programme _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, in particular creating and performing the character of 'Special Correspondent' Bob Hale (a parody of presenter [Peter Snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Peter_Snow "Peter Snow")).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-2) He has also appeared regularly on the spin-off game show _[Horrible Histories: Gory Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories:\_Gory\_Games "Horrible Histories: Gory Games")_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-3) and in the _Horrible Histories_[BBC Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_Proms "BBC Proms") at the Royal Albert Hall.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-4)

Along with the five other members of the _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ starring cast, Rickard is also the co-creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family/fantasy/comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013. A second series was released in 2015 and a third was commissioned and began filming in early 2016.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-5) In addition he is the co-writer of _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film which is based loosely around the early life of William Shakespeare and involves the same starring troupe.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-6) Filming took place in 2014, and the film had a nationwide UK release in September 2015.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-7)

As a performer, Rickard has also appeared in the Channel Four [Comedy Lab](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Comedy_Lab "Comedy Lab")_Private Lives_ as well as the TV series _[Balls of Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Balls\_of\_Steel\_(TV\_series) "Balls of Steel (TV series)")_. He is also a writer and performer on _[Tracey Ullman's Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Ullman's\_Show "Tracey Ullman's Show")_[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-8) and _[Tracey Breaks the News](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Tracey\_Breaks\_the\_News "Tracey Breaks the News")_. Rickard co-created, wrote, and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_ (2019-2023)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1) and is co-writer of the BBC sitcom _[Amandaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Amandaland "Amandaland")_ (2025-2026).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-9)

In 2024, Rickard was awarded an honorary doctorate in humanities from [Brunel University London](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Brunel_University_London "Brunel University London") for his services to television and education.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Laurence_Rickard#cite_note-brunel-1)

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the [Them There](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Them_There "Them There") collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest\_v1/page/html/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)
